purpose: Turn real gaps in the dataset into things a volunteer can usefully go and do.
principle: A quest must point at a gap that actually exists in the stored data. Inventing errands to keep people busy wastes their afternoon and teaches them not to trust the app.
Every quest says in one plain sentence why it is worth doing, naming the real fact behind it - the date of the last visit, the rain that fell, the season that is missing.
Quests are never ranked by how many a person completes. See data/points_rules.json for why volume is not rewarded.

rules.name: Nobody has been here for a while
rules.plain_language_condition: The site has been visited before, but not in the last 30 days.
rules.why_template: The last check here was {days} days ago, on {last_date}. A fresh look shows whether anything has changed since.

thresholds.source_note: A month is long enough that vegetation, flow and litter can all have changed, and short enough that a volunteer can reasonably be asked to return. No published standard sets a revisit interval for citizen stream assessment.

rules.name: Check after the rain
rules.plain_language_condition: Heavy rain has fallen here in the last 48 hours AND somebody has previously reported sewage or a discharging pipe at this site.
rules.why_template: {rain} mm of rain fell here in the last two days, and this site has {reports} report(s) of sewage or a discharging pipe. A check now shows whether it overflowed.
inputs: Open-Meteo, precipitation already observed in the last 48 hours
citizen-confirmed answers: sewage = Y or pollutedPipes = Y

thresholds.source_note: Set below the sewer-overflow alert threshold of 20 mm on purpose. The alert warns people away; this quest asks somebody to go and look, and it is worth looking at a lower bar than it is worth warning at. Neither figure is calibrated to any real network.
One prior report is enough to make a post-rain check worthwhile.
Three months: a site with a known pipe problem stays worth rechecking after rain for longer than the problem stays visible.

rules.name: This season has no record
rules.plain_language_condition: The site has been visited before, but never in the season we are in now.
rules.why_template: Nobody has seen {site} in {season}. Streams look very different across the year, and the record here has a {season} gap.
inputs: stored observations for the site, by calendar season

thresholds.source_note: Seasons are the meteorological quarters (Dec-Feb, Mar-May, Jun-Aug, Sep-Nov) for the northern hemisphere, where all five research cities are.

rules.name: A second opinion would help
rules.plain_language_condition: A recent assessment here was made by only one person.
rules.why_template: One person assessed {site} on {last_date}. A second pair of eyes makes the record much stronger, and disagreement is useful data in itself.
inputs: stored observations for the site, by pseudonymous client id

thresholds.source_note: Two independent assessments of the same site within a short window are what make inter-observer agreement measurable at all.
Two weeks, so the second visitor is describing roughly the same stream as the first.
